title: Whole-mount immunofluorescence imaging and isolation of mesothelium-bound immune cell aggregates during mouse peritoneal inflammation
protocol: Euthanize mice by CO2 inhalation.
Place the mouse on its back on a dissection board.
Spray the abdomen with 70% ethanol.
Make an incision in the skin in the abdominal area, starting in the lower abdominal midline and extending until the ribcage without penetrating the abdominal wall.
Extend the incision to the hind and forelegs.
Dissect the whole peritoneal wall using straight sharp scissors and 45° angled serrated forceps.
Transfer the peritoneal wall to a 60-mm Petri dish.
Flatten and stretch out the peritoneal wall on the bottom of the Petri dish using standard straight serrated forceps.
Ensure that the side of the peritoneal wall facing the peritoneal cavity is placed upwards during immunofluorescence staining.
Add 5 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde solution to the Petri dish.
Incubate at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Wash in PBS for 5 minutes.
Wash again in PBS for 5 minutes.
Cut the peritoneal wall along the midline into two halves.
Trim the edges so each half can fit into a well of a 12-well plate.
Dissect the omentum by lifting the liver up and isolating it from associated tissues using angled serrated and fine serrated forceps.
Transfer the dissected omentum to a well containing 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde solution.
Incubate for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Wash twice in PBS for 5 minutes each.
Transfer fixed samples to PBS and store overnight (12-16 hours) at 4°C before immunofluorescence staining.
Transfer peritoneal wall samples to wells of a 12-well plate for immunofluorescence staining.
Transfer peritoneal wall sample to a μ-Dish 35 mm dish with No. 1.5 ibidi Polymer Coverslip containing 300 μL of mowiol-based WMI mounting solution.
Mount peritoneal wall sample in a μ-Dish 35 mm dish with No. 1.5 ibidi Polymer Coverslip, and place an aluminum weight on top.
Place the mounted peritoneal wall sample with aluminum weight on top onto the stage of a confocal microscope.

Stain resMØ-aggregate in the peritoneal wall using Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-podoplanin, Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-F4/80, and unconjugated anti-fibrinogen followed by Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody.
Acquire WMI/confocal microscopy images of the stained resMØ-aggregate using a multispectral Leica TCS SP8 confocal microscope.
Analyze acquired images using ImageJ software.
Incubate each sample in 1 mL PBS 2% BSA for 30 min at 4°C for blocking unspecific binding of primary antibodies.
Incubate each sample in 1 mL of fluorophore-conjugated antibodies, diluted as indicated, in antibody staining solution, for 2–4 h at 4°C.
Wash samples twice in PBS for 5 min.
Incubate samples with unconjugated antibodies diluted as indicated in PBS 2% BSA for 2 hours at 4°C.
Wash samples twice in PBS for 5 minutes.
Incubate samples with secondary antibodies in antibody staining solution for 2 hours at 4°C.
For intracellular molecule staining, incubate samples with 0.1% Triton X-100 for 15 minutes at 4°C before antibody incubation.
Transfer peritoneal wall or omentum samples to μ-Dish 35 mm dishes containing No. 1.5 ibidi Polymer Coverslip and 300 μL of mowiol-based WMI mounting solution.
Place samples carefully in the dish to avoid formation of bubbles.
Place an aluminum weight on top of each sample to flatten and press against the bottom of the dish.
Make an incision in the skin in the abdominal area, starting in the lower abdominal midline, without penetrating the abdominal wall, and extend the incision until the neck.
Extend the incision to the hind and forelegs and remove all the abdominal and thoracic skin.
Inject 6–9 mL of cold PBS into the peritoneal cavity at the lower left quadrant of the abdomen using a 10 mL syringe with a 25 G needle.
Massage the abdomen vigorously to detach resMØ-aggregates from the mesothelium.
Make an incision in the peritoneal wall starting in the lower abdominal midline and extend the incision until the ribcage.
Incise the peritoneal wall.
Inject 8 mL PBS intraperitoneally.
Perform a peritoneal massage.
Harvest resMØ-aggregates.
Sediment harvested resMØ-aggregates at 4 h after E. coli infection.
Transfer resMØ-aggregates into a well of a flat-bottom 96-well plate.

Immunofluorescently stain resMØ-aggregates with PE-Cy7-conjugated anti-CD11b, APC-Cy7-conjugated anti-F4/80, APC-conjugated anti-MHC II, PE-conjugated anti-Ly6G, PE-conjugated anti-CD19, Pacific Blue-conjugated anti-B220 and PE-conjugated anti-CD90.
Acquire flow cytometry data on a Becton Dickinson LSR II flow cytometer.
Analyze flow cytometry data using FlowJo X software.
Stain the peritoneal wall with DAPI to detect resMØ-aggregates at 4 h after E. coli infection.
Obtain semithin sections of the peritoneal wall at 4 h after E. coli infection.
Perform Toluidine blue staining on semithin sections.
Collect peritoneal lavage containing resMØ-aggregates into a 15 mL Falcon tube using a glass funnel.
Place the tube on ice and allow resMØ-aggregates to sediment for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant carefully, leaving 0.5 mL with resMØ-aggregates at the bottom of the tube.
Add 5 mL of cold PBS.
Repeat steps involving centrifugation and removal of supernatant as needed to clean resMØ-aggregates of free cells.
Check quality of resMØ-aggregate preparation under an inverted phase contrast microscope after transferring into a well of a flat-bottom 96-well plate.
Transfer isolated resMØ-aggregates using a 200 μL micropipette with tips in which the front end has been cut off to avoid disruption.
Keep isolated resMØ-aggregates in 1 mL PBS in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge the isolated resMØ-aggregates preparation obtained in step 16 at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Add 500 μL of the enzymatic digestion solution and incubate in a waterbath at 37°C for 5 min.
Disrupt resMØ-aggregates mechanically by gentle pipetting using a 200 μL micropipette.
Transfer the cell suspension into a well of a flat-bottom 96-well plate to check resMØ-aggregate disruption under an inverted phase contrast microscope.
Add 10 mL PBS-EDTA-FBS to stop the enzymatic digestion.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend in 500 μL PBS-EDTA-FBS.
Transfer cells obtained from step 23 into a 96-well V-bottom plate at ≥105 cells/well.
Centrifuge the 96-well plate at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant, resuspend the cells in 30 μL of anti-CD16/32 antibody to block Fc receptors.
Incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Wash with 100 μL PBS-EDTA-FBS per well and centrifuge at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant, resuspend the cells in 30 μL of fluorophore-conjugated antibodies diluted in PBS-EDTA-FBS.
Incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Wash with 100 μL PBS-EDTA-FBS per well and centrifuge at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant, resuspend in 200 μL PBS-EDTA-FBS.
Transfer the cells to 5 mL polypropylene tubes.
Transfer isolated resMØ-aggregates into a 1.5 mL eppendorf tube.
Add 0.5 mL of Fixation Solution for Electron Microscopy.
Incubate overnight at 4°C.
Remove the Fixation Solution and wash twice with 1 mL HEPES 0.15 M buffer for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove HEPES 0.15 M buffer and wash four times with 1 mL cacodylate buffer 0.1 M for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Incubate with 0.5 mL osmium tetroxide solution for 1 hour at 4°C in the dark.
Remove osmium tetroxide solution and wash four times with 1 mL cacodylate buffer 0.1 M for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Wash twice with 1 mL ddH2O for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Incubate with 0.5 mL uranyl acetate solution for 60 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Remove uranyl acetate solution and wash twice with 1 mL ddH2O for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Incubate with 1 mL 70% acetone for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Incubate with 1 mL 90% acetone for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Incubate with 1 mL 100% acetone for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Exchange 100% acetone and incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Incubate in 1 mL 1:1 epoxy resin/100% acetone for 30 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Exchange epoxy resin and incubate for 2 hours at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Exchange epoxy resin again and incubate for 3 hours at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Transfer the peritoneal wall to a 60-mm Petri dish containing 5 mL of Fixation Solution for Electron Microscopy and incubate overnight (12–16 h) at 4°C.
Remove the Fixation Solution and wash twice with 5 mL PBS for 5 min at 4°C.
Cut the peritoneal wall in two halves and trim edges so each fits in a well of a 12-well plate.
Incubate samples with 5 mL DAPI at 1:200 in PBS for 15 min at 4°C in the dark.
Remove DAPI and wash with PBS for 5 min at 4°C.
Transfer peritoneal wall samples to μ-Dish 35 mm dishes with No. 1.5 ibidi Polymer Coverslip containing 300 μL of PBS.
Place an aluminum weight on top of each sample.
Analyze the samples by confocal microscopy to locate resMØ-aggregates.
Remove the aluminum weight carefully.
Determine the position of the piece of peritoneal wall using the vasculature as a reference.
Dissect small pieces (∼2 × 2 mm) of peritoneal wall containing the defined zones.
Transfer the dissected peritoneal wall pieces into a 1.5 mL eppendorf tube.
Follow steps 31c to 31q for processing.
Prepare semithin sections of the selected areas.
Confirm the presence of resMØ-aggregates in the semithin sections prior to electron microscopy studies.
